quote: You become responsible, forever, for what you have tamed.
source: Antoine de Saint-Exupéry, The Little Prince, chapter XXI (the fox) (trans. Katherine Woods, 1943)

evidence.where: A scanned copy of the Katherine Woods translation (title page names her), the fox chapter read in full; the chapter number rests on the standard numbering of the book, since the scan carries page numbers rather than chapter heads
evidence.edition: The Little Prince, trans. Katherine Woods (Reynal & Hitchcock, New York, 1943)
evidence.locator: Chapter XXI, the fox’s farewell: “Men have forgotten this truth,” said the fox. “But you must not forget it. You become responsible, forever, for what you have tamed. You are responsible for your rose . . .”

speaker: The fox
reason: Woods’s wording is exactly as proposed and is the fox’s own line in the taming chapter; the French is “Tu deviens responsable pour toujours de ce que tu as apprivoisé.” Not shipped, person unused, not banned.
